variants.headline: Looking back: party names a new leader
variants.sub: Leadership of {party} has changed, with {new} the new leader.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: The party {party} had a new leader: {new}.

The gazette records the change of party leadership without presuming the circumstances in which it occurred. The replacement of a leader does not establish a resignation, a dismissal or an internal contest unless those particulars are separately known. A precise notice should avoid supplying them by implication.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. New leadership deserves the opportunity for a fair hearing, and recognition of that opportunity need not depend on inventing achievements before they occur.

variants.headline: Looking back: leadership changes hands
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: Leadership of {party} had changed, with {new} the new leader.

The gazette records the change of party leadership without presuming the circumstances in which it occurred. The replacement of a leader does not establish a resignation, a dismissal or an internal contest unless those particulars are separately known. A precise notice should avoid supplying them by implication.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. New leadership deserves the opportunity for a fair hearing, and recognition of that opportunity need not depend on inventing achievements before they occur.

variants.headline: Looking back: a new name at the head of the party
variants.sub: The party {party} has a new leader: {new}.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: The new leader of {party} was {new}.

The gazette records the change of party leadership without presuming the circumstances in which it occurred. The replacement of a leader does not establish a resignation, a dismissal or an internal contest unless those particulars are separately known. A precise notice should avoid supplying them by implication.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. New leadership deserves the opportunity for a fair hearing, and recognition of that opportunity need not depend on inventing achievements before they occur.
